steps.title: Import React and hooks from 'react'
steps.instruction: Import React, useState, useEffect, and useCallback from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use a single import statement to bring in all four items from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing React and hooks
import React, { useState, useEffect, useCallback } from 'react';
steps.seedCode: // Import React and hooks from 'react' here
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have an import statement that brings React, useState, useEffect, and useCallback into your file.
successCriteria: The import statement must import React, useState, useEffect, and useCallback from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and the necessary hooks. This gives us the building blocks for creating our custom hook.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing all four items: React, useState, useEffect, and useCallback from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: This step requires importing React, useState, useEffect, and useCallback from 'react'. Please try again.

steps.title: Define the Permission type
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript type alias named 'Permission' that is a string union type with the values 'read', 'write', and 'delete'.
steps.hint: Use the 'type' keyword followed by the type name and the union syntax with pipe (|) characters between the string literal values.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of defining a string union type
type Status = 'active' | 'inactive' | 'pending';
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a type definition that can be used to type-check permission values throughout the application.
successCriteria: The code must include a type alias named 'Permission' that is a union of the three string literal types: 'read', 'write', and 'delete'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the Permission type as a string union. This will help ensure type safety when working with permission values.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check your syntax. Make sure you're using the 'type' keyword, the correct name 'Permission', and the pipe (|) operator between the three string values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Permission type definition is missing or incorrect. You need to create a type alias that represents a union of the three string literal values: 'read', 'write', and 'delete'.

steps.title: Define the UserRole type
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript type alias named 'UserRole' as a string union type with the values 'admin', 'editor', and 'viewer'.
steps.hint: Use the 'type' keyword to create a type alias. String union types use the pipe (|) operator to combine multiple string literal values.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of a string union type
type Status = 'pending' | 'active' | 'inactive';
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a UserRole type that can only be 'admin', 'editor', or 'viewer'.
successCriteria: The code must include a type alias named 'UserRole' that is a string union of exactly 'admin', 'editor', and 'viewer'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the UserRole type as a string union. This will help enforce valid role values throughout your application.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're creating a type alias (not an interface) and that it includes all three string values: 'admin', 'editor', and 'viewer'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The UserRole type definition is missing or incorrect. Remember to use the 'type' keyword and create a string union with 'admin', 'editor', and 'viewer'.

steps.title: Define the rolePermissions mapping
steps.instruction: Define a constant named 'rolePermissions' that maps each UserRole to an array of Permission values. Use the UserRole and Permission types you defined earlier.
steps.hint: Create a TypeScript object where keys are UserRole values and values are arrays of Permission values.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a rolePermissions object that clearly defines which permissions each user role has.
successCriteria: The code should include a constant named 'rolePermissions' that is an object with UserRole keys and Permission array values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the rolePermissions mapping. This provides the foundation for checking permissions based on user roles.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure 'rolePermissions' is defined as a constant object with proper TypeScript typing using the UserRole and Permission types.
steps.feedbackWrong: The rolePermissions mapping wasn't defined correctly. Remember to create a constant object where keys are UserRole values and values are arrays of Permission values.

steps.title: Create the useRBAC hook function
steps.instruction: Create a custom hook function named 'useRBAC' that takes a 'role' parameter of type UserRole and returns an object. The function should be empty for now (just return an empty object).
steps.hint: Define a function with the name useRBAC that accepts a role parameter typed as UserRole and returns an object. You can use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax.
steps.expectedOutcome: A useRBAC function is created with the correct signature (takes UserRole parameter, returns object).
successCriteria: Function named useRBAC exists
Function takes one parameter named 'role'
Parameter 'role' is typed as UserRole
Function returns an object (empty for now)
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the basic structure of the useRBAC hook with the correct TypeScript signature.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Check that your function: 1) is named 'useRBAC', 2) takes a 'role' parameter of type 'UserRole', and 3) returns an object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The useRBAC hook function isn't quite right. Make sure you create a function named 'useRBAC' that accepts a 'role' parameter (typed as UserRole) and returns an object.

steps.title: Initialize the permissions state
steps.instruction: Inside the useRBAC hook function, use useState to create a state variable named 'permissions' initialized to an empty array of type Permission[].
steps.hint: Use the useState hook with a generic type parameter <Permission[]> and pass an empty array [] as the initial value.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of initializing a state variable with an empty array
const [items, setItems] = useState<string[]>([]);
steps.expectedOutcome: The useRBAC hook will have a permissions state variable that can hold an array of Permission values.
successCriteria: The code should include a useState call inside useRBAC that declares a 'permissions' variable with type Permission[] and initializes it to an empty array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the permissions state variable. This will allow the hook to track which permissions the current user has.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check: Did you use useState with the correct generic type <Permission[]>? Is the state variable named 'permissions'? Is it initialized to an empty array []?
steps.feedbackWrong: The permissions state hasn't been properly initialized. Remember to use useState<Permission[]>([]) inside the useRBAC function to create a state variable named 'permissions'.

steps.title: Create the updatePermissions function
steps.instruction: Inside the useRBAC function, create a function named 'updatePermissions' that takes a 'role' parameter of type UserRole and updates the permissions state based on the rolePermissions mapping.
steps.hint: Define a function inside useRBAC that uses the role parameter to look up permissions from rolePermissions and calls the setPermissions state setter.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useRBAC hook now contains an updatePermissions function that can update permissions based on a role parameter.
successCriteria: The code should include a function named 'updatePermissions' inside useRBAC that takes a 'role' parameter of type UserRole and updates the permissions state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the updatePermissions function. This function will be essential for updating permissions whenever the user's role changes.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your updatePermissions function takes a 'role' parameter of type UserRole and properly updates the permissions state using setPermissions.
steps.feedbackWrong: The updatePermissions function is missing or incorrect. Remember to create a function inside useRBAC that accepts a role parameter and updates the permissions state.

steps.title: Add useEffect to update permissions on role change
steps.instruction: Inside the useRBAC hook, add a useEffect hook that will update permissions when the role changes. The useEffect should call updatePermissions with the current role.
steps.hint: Use the useEffect hook from React. The dependency array should include the role variable.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useRBAC hook now includes a useEffect that will trigger permission updates when the role changes.
successCriteria: useEffect is called inside useRBAC
useEffect has a dependency array
useEffect calls updatePermissions
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the useEffect hook. This will ensure permissions are updated whenever the role changes.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your useEffect includes the role in its dependency array and calls updatePermissions inside.
steps.feedbackWrong: The useEffect hook is missing or incorrectly implemented. Remember to add useEffect inside useRBAC with the role as a dependency.

steps.title: Create the hasPermission function
steps.instruction: Inside the useRBAC hook, create a function named 'hasPermission' that takes a parameter of type Permission and returns a boolean indicating whether that permission exists in the permissions array.
steps.hint: You can use the array 'includes' method to check if the permission parameter exists in the permissions state array.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useRBAC hook should now contain a hasPermission function that can check if a specific permission is allowed.
successCriteria: Function named 'hasPermission' exists
Function takes a parameter of type 'Permission'
Function returns a boolean
Function checks if permission exists in 'permissions' array
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the hasPermission helper function. This function will be essential for checking individual permissions in your RBAC system.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your hasPermission function: 1) Takes a parameter of type Permission, 2) Returns a boolean, and 3) Checks if that permission exists in the permissions array using the 'includes' method.
steps.feedbackWrong: The hasPermission function is missing or incorrect. Remember to create a function inside useRBAC that takes a Permission parameter and returns true/false based on whether that permission is in the permissions array.

steps.title: Return the hook's interface
steps.instruction: Return an object from the useRBAC hook containing the permissions array and hasPermission function so they can be used by components.
steps.hint: At the end of your hook function, use the return keyword followed by an object with permissions and hasPermission properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useRBAC hook now returns an object with permissions and hasPermission, making these values available to any component that calls the hook.
successCriteria: The hook returns an object
The object contains a permissions property
The object contains a hasPermission property
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've successfully returned the hook's interface. Components can now destructure { permissions, hasPermission } from useRBAC() to access these values.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're returning an object with both permissions and hasPermission properties from the hook.
steps.feedbackWrong: The hook needs to return an object containing both permissions and hasPermission so components can use them.

steps.title: Use the hook in the component and display permissions
steps.instruction: Inside the PermissionDemo component, call the useRBAC hook with a role of 'editor', then return JSX that displays the permissions array and tests hasPermission for different permission types.
steps.hint: Call the hook at the top of your component, then use the returned values to render information about permissions.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will display the permissions array for the 'editor' role and show whether specific permissions are granted.
successCriteria: Call useRBAC with 'editor' as the role
Display the permissions array in JSX
Test hasPermission for at least two different permission types
